slides.title: Real-World Data Feeds Real-World Evidence
bullets: The FDA defines real-world data as routinely collected patient health information
Sources include electronic health records, disease registries, insurance claims, wearables and patient-reported data
Real-world evidence is the clinical evidence on a product's use, benefits or risks derived from that data

slides.title: A Data Source, Not a Design
bullets: RWE isn't a single study design, it's a data source that can feed several designs
It can feed cohort studies, administrative database analyses, patient registries or pragmatic trials
Traditional RCTs run in selected populations, over limited time, under controlled conditions
RWE shows how a treatment behaves across real patient diversity and over longer follow-up

slides.title: Agencies Have Built RWE Into Decision-Making
bullets: The FDA has had a formal framework for using RWE in regulatory decisions since 2018
It has long supported postmarketing safety surveillance
It increasingly informs effectiveness decisions, indication expansions and comparative study design
The EMA follows a similar path through DARWIN EU, its European real-world data network

slides.title: The Questions Only RWE Can Answer
bullets: How does this treatment perform in patients over 75 with renal impairment
What real-world persistence does it show outside the trial
How does it compare to the alternative in daily hospital practice
RWE also surfaces evidence gaps that can become new studies or research collaborations

slides.title: RWE Still Needs Critical Appraisal
bullets: Question the source and quality of the underlying data
Check the statistical adjustment used to control confounding
Assess how representative the population is
Look for transparent methodology, following frameworks like ISPOR or STROBE

takeaway.title: Real-world evidence shows how treatments perform outside the controlled trial setting
bullets: RWE is a data source, not a study design, and can feed many different analyses
Regulators now use it for safety surveillance and, increasingly, effectiveness decisions
It still demands the same critical questions about data quality, adjustment and representativeness
